claim: AC1: a payload from _build_table_payload with 1 row, 1 column and truncated==0 becomes exactly one text block `**<column>:** <value>` and no table block.
AC2: a 1-row payload with 2-4 columns and truncated==0 becomes one text block, a bullet list with one `- **col:** value` item per column in column order, and no table block.
AC3: a payload with 2 or more rows produces the same table block as before.
AC4: a payload with 1 row and 5+ columns produces the same table block as before.
AC5: a 1-row result with truncated==1 (row dropped by size budget) still produces the same table block as before.

AC6: the text block for a qualifying one-row result sits at the same position in `blocks` that its table block used to occupy, relative to text and chart blocks (including through the total-budget trimming pass).
AC7: each value in the text block is the same _coerce_cell output the table cell held, before escaping.
AC8: each of \ ` * _ [ ] < > ~ | & in a column name or value gets a preceding backslash, and each CR/LF becomes one space, so `*x* [a](b)` renders literally.
AC9: two qualifying one-row results in one turn each become their own text block at their own stream position (no merging).
AC10: for a qualifying one-row result, the Markdown answer in the tool result's text content (query_database_impl_with_widgets) contains the `**col:** value` lines and no Markdown table.
AC11: query_info.row_count == 1 for a turn whose last query returned 1 row with at most 4 columns.

AC12: the default-tool system prompt drops the old 'raw result is shown to the user outside of your response so YOU DO NOT need to include it' sentence; says multi-row results are shown as a table not to repeat and a one-row result is stated in a plain sentence; and no other line (incl. emit_text rules) says a one-row result is shown as a table or should not be stated.

The Response Guidelines line tells the model to 'state the answer in a plain sentence in your response', while with emit_text present non-emit_text text is hidden; check the prompt does not give conflicting instructions so that the one-row answer would be hidden when emit_text is in the tool set.

claim: The widget renders the escaped `**col:** value` text via renderTextBlock (markdown-it html:false, breaks:true), and the backslash escapes (including \< \& \|) come out as literal characters. The new comment above createMarkdownRenderer states this accurately.
verify_against: markdown-it backslash-escape rules (CommonMark ASCII punctuation escapes) and renderTextBlock
verify_hint: renderTextBlock/createMarkdownRenderer in query_results.html; CommonMark escape rules for & and |
evidence:
src/sqllens/ui/query_results.html:752-753 createMarkdownRenderer configures markdown-it with {html:false, linkify:false, typographer:false, breaks:true}; renderTextBlock (line 772-785) uses this renderer via container.innerHTML = markdownRenderer.render(text). src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:47-49 defines _SMALL_RESULT_ESCAPED_CHARS = frozenset("\\`*_[]<>~|&") and _escape_small_result_text (line 1192-1196) backslash-escapes those chars, used to build '**col:** value' lines (line 1218). Empirically ran the actual vendored markdown-it.min.js with the same options against text containing \\< \\& \\| and confirmed the rendered output is '

col: a<b&c|d

' - i.e. literal <, &, | characters in the rendered HTML, not parsed as markdown/HTML syntax, consistent with CommonMark's ASCII-punctuation backslash-escape rule. The comment block above createMarkdownRenderer (lines 739-751) accurately describes html:false as the XSS boundary and notes the text is backslash-escaped by tools/_format.py, without overstating anything false.
